backbone: A cyclic-group colouring built from Behrend-type squared-norm geometry plus random bits (finite local lemma) and a sparse random perturbation avoids monochromatic k-APs, then transfers to intervals and r colours.
quote: Assign to every $\beta\in\cL$ an independent uniform random bit $\xi_\beta$. We introduce two finite families of bad events.

backbone: Explicit 35-vertex incidence graph H; a rank-layer random-matrix model over F_q yields a kernel with negative correlation as q grows, then dilution and sampling give a finite host G.
quote: Let \(H\) be the incidence graph of the \(22\) triples on \(13\) points in Table~\ref{tab:complex}. This bipartite graph has \(35\) vertices and \(66\) edges.

backbone: Hypergraph from modified line partitions of F_q^2 with randomly selected merged/split lines; a small cover is forced into a pencil (Szonyi-Weiner stability) and exhausted by incidence counts.
quote: Under uniform deletion of a fixed number of lines per direction, with probability tending to one every small core cover also covers almost all of the whole plane.

backbone: Ramsey/finite-sums selection fixes product colours; Prediction (nilsequence models via inverse theorem) and Alignment (random scale choice with probability bounded below) keep sums the same colour.
quote: Alignment selects from a fixed finite list of rational scale vectors so that a positive prediction at every center remains positive after all the required additive shifts. Its success probability is bounded below

backbone: Signed intersection cycle pairing turns a drawing into linear-algebraic data; a polynomial-interpolation subspace inequality bounds crossings below by Z(n), matched by the classical drawings.
quote: The proof separates the geometry of a drawing from two linear-algebraic statements.

backbone: Take the least dimension where the bound fails; polynomial interpolation on selected direction stars, secant/variety degree bounds and rigid-motion incidence (Guth-Katz input) yield a contradiction.
quote: Suppose that Theorem~\ref{thm:main} fails, and take the least dimension \(d\ge3\) in which it fails.

backbone: Assuming failure, extract an extremal graph of large distance fibers, build nested arithmetic partitions with an overlap identity, and exclude both scale regimes via variance and limiting fiber maps.
quote: Assuming that Theorem~\ref{thm:main} fails, we first choose a sequence with nearly maximal density of pairs in large distance fibers.

backbone: Simultaneous induction on interval rank proves KL-polynomial invariance together with freeness of moment-graph sheaf kernels along a transported reflection-order schedule, via dihedral localization.
quote: We prove polynomial invariance simultaneously with freeness of $L_u(F)$ for every terminal portion $F$ at the bottom. The induction is on interval rank

backbone: Identify elementary coefficients with positive quantum-torus/scattering-diagram objects via positive reordering and wall transport, then realize the identities by an explicit permutation witness procedure.
quote: It first identifies each relevant elementary coefficient with a positive algebraic object. It then realizes the algebraic identities by finite bijections between ordered collections of independent sets.

backbone: Lower bound: random incident point-hyperplane flags in PG(s-1,q) give a K_s-free ordered graph; small independence number by an entropy compression contradiction with dimension induction. Upper bound classical.
quote: A position receives a random incident pair \((a,b)\), where \(a\) is a point of \(\PG(4,q)\) and \(b\) is a hyperplane containing it.

backbone: Assume a bad sequence of colourings; stabilize discrepancy across widths through phases, then embed a monochromatic cube via probabilistic rows, lopsided local lemma and Hall's theorem, contradiction.
quote: We prove Theorem~\ref{thm:main} by contradiction along sequences.

backbone: Necessity: failure of the tensor condition yields an explicit modular colouring. Sufficiency: group-path endpoints with Hales-Jewett, ultrafilter products and compactness force a monochromatic copy.
quote: After fixing the Hales--Jewett word length $n$, we prepare one endpoint at weights $1,1/2,\ldots,1/n$ before coloring the words. An ultrafilter construction then realizes the products by finite strings, keeping common factors identical.

backbone: Minimal counterexample gives a strict subset inequality; blow-up by transitive tournaments and a pruning bound for binary relations yield an extremal contradiction.
quote: We first suppose that a counterexample exists and choose one with minimum order and then minimum number of arcs.

backbone: Extract a low-resistance tree packing via hierarchy shortcuts and a fixed-point argument, then iterate a spectral sparsification step (interlacing/barrier) until a thin spanning tree remains.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:iteration} combines the two representations, iterates the sparsification, and proves the binary-multiplicity reduction.

backbone: Given a cheap fractional cover, suppose F is not p-small; the multiscale selector estimate on random colourings gives a member contradicting the fractional cover budget.
quote: Suppose, for a contradiction, that $\mathcal F$ is not $p$-small.

backbone: Reduce containment to covering a disjoint probability tree; repeated fresh random sets each halve level capacities (one simultaneous reduction per round) until a path is covered.
quote: Start with $\TT$ and make successive attempts using fresh independent sets of law $\mu_\rho$.

backbone: Explicit coset complexes of a congruence subgroup of SL_N(k[t]) and their finite congruence quotients; acyclicity via twin buildings and homological stability, then the KMS criterion gives expansion.
quote: We construct an infinite $n$-dimensional coset complex $L$ for $U$ and its finite congruence quotients $T_m$. The desired $X_m$ is the $d$-skeleton of $T_m$.

backbone: A deterministic algorithm pairs stubs in stages (pair most, cleanup, complete), derandomizing choices with resolvent/moment estimates, then a biased switch repair makes the spectrum exactly Ramanujan.
quote: For every fixed integer d ≥ 3, we give a deterministic algorithm that constructs a simple nonbipartite d-regular Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number n of vertices.

backbone: Suppose another order exists; cyclotomic divisibility and descent at 2 force order 4u^2, then character values in local cyclotomic rings and a binary coefficient identity give a contradiction.
quote: Suppose there were an example of another order. By Proposition~\ref{prop:order}, its order is \(4u^2\) with \(u>1\) odd.

backbone: Dualize to partitioning a 2-face-coloured triangulation into two induced trees; induct on vertices across separating triangles, with base case from a pair of disjoint Tutte states via weighted cancellation.
quote: Induct on the number of vertices, using the construction above when there is no separating triangle.

backbone: Strong induction on n with multiscale splitting: one expanding layer pays for a prefix of scales via pair folding and path closing, with a phi(n) bound absorbing overhead.
quote: We use strong induction on \(n\).

backbone: Reflection-positive tuple laws give a multilinear form dominating a power of density; circle-method comparison shows it contracts on shorter progressions, and the contracting recurrence yields the power saving.
quote: The square-difference method constructs a multilinear form which dominates a fixed power of density, and proves that this form contracts on passing to shorter intervals.

backbone: A uniform little-o improvement of the activity-packing bound, proved by contradiction through limiting rank-coordinate measures and transverse foliations, gives a contracting recurrence and the power saving.
quote: We prove a uniform little-$o$ improvement of this packing bound as $n/b$ tends to infinity. Choosing one sufficiently large fixed scale then gives a contracting recurrence and the power saving

backbone: Iterated small random colouring rounds with entry weights; a local weight-adjustment lemma (vertex splitting, walk entropy) controls triangle mass and keeps lists rich until colouring completes.
quote: The proof constructs a partial coloring in small random rounds.

backbone: Construct (transfinite recursion with an ultrafilter ordinal rank) a self-dual matroid Q, chain copies along a double ray into M0,M1; an independent covering would give a strictly descending ordinal sequence.
quote: To build the pair, join consecutive integer vertices by \emph{bundles}, each a labelled copy of $D$, and place $Q$ on the two incident bundles at each vertex.

backbone: Biased Fourier expansion: influence controls high-degree mass; restricting to a random vertex block and symmetry plus a hypercontractive low-degree estimate bound remaining mass, then Russo's formula gives width.
quote: Thus the influence controls high degrees. The task is to bound the remaining mass using symmetry.

backbone: An explicit Maker policy from a certificate of 728 combined conditional winning positions (proof tree), verified finitely by computer, completes Snaky within 21 moves.
quote: there is one globally legal Maker policy that completes an allowed copy of $S$ within at most $21$ actual Maker claims against every legal continuation of Breaker.

backbone: Run to a good prefix (Joos-Kuhn estimates), then analyse the continuation by backward priority exploration, independent unfoldings with product identities, and coupling, giving second-moment convergence.
quote: The proof separates the part of the process governed by uniform subgraph counts from the final evolution of individual edges.

backbone: Minimal counterexample has neighbourhood expansion; a large-clique lemma and optimal path systems reduce to 3,099 finite pattern instances excluded by computer-implemented inference rules.
quote: The proof combines expansion in a minimal counterexample with a large-clique lemma and an optimization of paths joining clique vertices.

backbone: Explicit 66x66 pattern with a 64x64 anchor and tree-structured host matrices; copies are confined to leaf-diagonal cells (few) while distance to H-freeness stays large.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:construction} gives the pattern and the host entries explicitly.

backbone: Random integral columns modulo a prime power labelled by finite-field norms make small determinants rare; lattice counts bound bad pairs/triples, and deletion leaves n points.
quote: We construct random columns modulo a prime power, each carrying a label in a finite field.
